title: Tracing Antisemitic Language Through Diachronic Embedding Projections: France 1789-1914
findings: The study found a steady increase of adverse bias against Jews, particularly from the mid-1880s onwards, culminating in the Dreyfus affair. The highest level of adverse bias was detected in the religious semantic area, followed by the economic and ethic spheres. When compared to other religious groups, the term 'juif' (Jew) showed an exclusively adverse bias, whereas 'catholique' (Catholic) showed an entirely favorable bias. Adverse bias against Protestants and Muslims was also detected but was primarily concentrated within the religious domain and was less severe than the antisemitic bias.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the evolution of antisemitic bias in French texts from 1789-1914. It quantifies this bias by projecting word embeddings onto six different semantic axes: religious, economic, socio-political, racial, ethic, and conspiratorial. The religious axis specifically measures bias based on theological doctrines, narratives, and religious prejudices.
